description: Flat 4 x 8 m soi alley tile textured as a straight shared-surface alley with an open side drain down each edge -- one quad, one PBR texture set.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Rectangular section of narrow alley paved in worn concrete slabs, no kerb or separated sidewalk, an open rectangular drain channel running along each side under lift-out concrete lid slabs, low raised edge strip at the boundary Materials: Cracked and patched pale concrete slabs, damp dark staining along the drain lids, moss in the joints, oil spotting down the centre line where motorcycles run.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

name: Soi Alley Straight Tile
notes: One flat quad, 4 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. The entire surface reads out of the texture: paving, drain channels and lids, edge strips, markings and covers are painted into the maps, never built. The earlier procedural version of this tile modelled a raised edge strip and a recessed open drain channel and it did not work, so the flat quad replaces it outright -- there is no step up onto the edge strip and no recess in the drain, and the drain reads as a channel because of its albedo, normal and AO, not because there is a hole there. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the class its footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. Quality comes entirely from a high-end PBR texture generator -- albedo, roughness, normal and AO at photoreal fidelity matched to the reference plate -- and not from mesh detail; that is the whole bet of this piece. Fit is the one hard requirement. The footprint is exactly 4 x 8 m -- the kit's half-module on its 8 m grid, so a run of these lands on 8 m centres and a tile row lines up with the shophouse row that shares the grid. The pivot is base-center. Its edge profile is the kit's half-module alley: a 3 m paved alley with a 0.5 m edge band each side, all of it now flat at y=0. That profile mates only with the other alley pieces and with the branch edge of the Soi Entrance tile, which is the adapter back to the full 8 m road profile. The texture has to be edge-matched to the rest of the set at those band boundaries: surface tone, edge-strip position, drain-lid coursing and slab joints must continue across a seam without a visible join. No destruction groups: a road tile is static level geometry, not a breakable. A soi has no separated sidewalk -- pedestrians and motorcycles share one surface -- which is why this piece was always closer to a flat plane than a scaled-down road tile, and why it loses the least in becoming one. The open side drain under lift-out lid slabs is the defining feature of a Thai alley and reads at a glance from the far end of a run; with the recess gone, that read now depends entirely on the normal and AO maps carrying the lid joints and the dark channel line, so it is the thing to check first on the generated texture. This is the repeating piece of the alley set and will be instanced down the whole length of a soi, so a run of forty is forty draw calls off one shared geometry and one shared material.
